perspective:
From Gloria Bangura’s point of view, she has access to:

- She is an administrative assistant at a large event planning company.
- Donald Ortega is a colleague who works part-time as a bartender during company events; they are not personally close and interact mainly at those events.
- Over several company events, she directly observed Donald serving drinks without enthusiasm and seeming distracted.
- She approached Donald and asked if he was okay and if everything was all right with his job.
- Donald told her he was “not as into it” as he used to be and that the work felt repetitive.
- After reflecting on that conversation, she suspected his job dissatisfaction might point to deeper personal issues, so she suggested he consider talking to a professional.
- Donald told her he hadn’t really considered that and wasn’t sure it would help.
- She sensed a shift in Donald’s behavior toward her afterward and worried he resented her suggestion and felt she had overstepped.
- She apologized to Donald, explaining she only wanted to help and didn’t mean to make assumptions about his life.
- Donald told her he was initially taken aback, but he knew she meant well and said it was “a lot to process.”
- Feeling relieved that the tension had eased, she invited Donald to collaborate on an upcoming project and told him it could use his creative input.
- Donald accepted appreciatively and said it sounded like a great opportunity.
- During their collaboration, she observed Donald’s significant contributions and renewed enthusiasm.
- She concluded that Donald was a valuable team member and publicly acknowledged his work during a team meeting.
- Donald thanked her, said her recognition meant a lot to him, and said it felt great to be appreciated.
